subject: Call recap — budget runway, token levers & 6-week pilot ask
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@payproto.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Call recap — budget runway, token levers & 6-week pilot ask

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and to drive the next steps. Appreciate you walking us through PayProto’s priorities.

Key pain points you called out
- Token spend is the biggest friction: unpredictable spikes from peak reconciliation flows and the fraud model scoring creating the majority of tokens.
- Ops team needs a predictable monthly spend for FY27 planning; current ML infra costs are scoped as a variable hit to the payments P&L and need to be contained to the mid 5-figures / month range.
- Latency SLOs: customer-facing approval flows need sub-300ms 95th percentile for short text models; batch scoring for nightly jobs can tolerate higher latency.

Goals we aligned on
- Validate a 6-week pilot that demonstrates 50–100k monthly active tokens routing through Redwood with batching + prefix caching enabled for nightly jobs.
- Show unit cost reductions with batching and a conservative quantization profile while maintaining model accuracy within your current A/B thresholds.
- Produce an ROI snapshot for the payments team and a simple procurement path for procurement (SOW + pricing examples).

Immediate asks / next steps (owner in parentheses)
1) I’ll share a 6-week pilot workbook with three budget scenarios (conservative / target / upside) and recommended batching/cache settings (Irene).
2) Can you confirm a conservative pilot cap to model against? You mentioned ~80k tokens/month as a sweet spot — confirmation would help us size infra. (Alyssa)
3) Procurement: will PayProto need an NDA or standard PO first? If there’s a procurement contact, please loop them in so we can include required billing/legal items in the SOW. (Alyssa)
4) If you can share a small sample of the nightly batch profile (avg seq len, token distribution, peak hour window) that will let us refine latency/cost estimates. (Marissa)

Attachments: pilot workbook + pricing examples (stubs attached below).

I’ve CC’d Marissa to own the pilot workbook and the pricing examples attachment. We’ll aim to have a draft workbook and a short ROI slide by EOD Tuesday PT.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@payproto.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, PayProto Procurement <procure@payproto.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 17:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Call recap — budget runway, token levers & 6-week pilot ask

Thanks, Irene — super helpful. Confirming a few quick points:

- Pilot cap: we can run with a conservative cap of 75,000 tokens/month for the pilot. If the economics are promising, our finance lead has flexibility to expand to 200k/mo.
- Procurement: looped in procurement (procure@payproto.com). They’ll need the SOW + line-item pricing and a data-processing addendum (DPA).
- Sample data: I’ll pull a one-week extract of nightly batch runs (approx 3M tokens across the week, with most sequences 8–24 tokens, peaks between 02:00–03:00 local). Expect that in your inbox Monday morning.

Questions for your team: can you provide a ballpark effective per-1M-token cost for the three scenarios you mentioned (conservative / target / aggressive) including the effect of batching and prefix caching? We don’t need perfect numbers — just something we can show finance to get fast alignment.

Also — latency: happy to split the pilot into two tracks (1) customer-facing short text path with strict SLOs, (2) nightly batch scoring where we optimize for cost. Thoughts?

Best,
Alyssa
Head of ML Ops | PayProto
alyssa@payproto.com

On procurement: procurement, happy to meet for 20 min Monday if you need context on what the pilot buys from a technical lens.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@payproto.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Call recap — budget runway, token levers & 6-week pilot ask

Hi Alyssa / Irene —

Thanks for the context, Alyssa. I pulled together a fast back-of-envelope based on the 75k cap and the expected batch profile you mentioned. High-level:

- Conservative scenario (minimal batching, no prefix cache): ~ $1,200 / month effective for the pilot (~$16 per 1k tokens equivalence)
- Target scenario (batching enabled for nightly jobs, 2x effective batch factor, prefix caching for repeat prefixes): ~ $420 / month (~$5.6 per 1k tokens equivalence)
- Aggressive optimization (higher batch factor, 8-bit quantization on scoring model where acceptable): ~ $280 / month (~$3.7 per 1k tokens equivalence)

Assumptions: pilot uses a small customer-facing model for approvals (avg seq len 18 tokens) and a heavier model for fraud scoring in nightly batch (avg seq len 42). We assumed 75k tokens across the month distributed 60% nightly batch / 40% interactive.

Irene — attached is the pilot workbook with the scenario tabs and a one-page ROI summary for PayProto’s finance review. The pricing examples PDF shows line-item pricing we use in SOWs for pilots (reserve vs on-demand, burst policies).

Next operational asks to keep momentum:
- Alyssa/procurement: confirm DPA needs and whether you require a vendor questionnaire before we start the SOW.
- Alyssa: confirm which model family we should baseline experiments on (your current in-house model or the open checkpoint we suggested).
- PayProto: a PO or signed SOW (we can start with a provisional PO for the pilot amount).

If it helps, Karthik can join the procurement sync to go over SLA, data handling, and pricing structure. He’s looped here.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks,
Alyssa
